=== FINDINGS (none blocking; verdict AGREE) ===
F1 -- REAL, INTRODUCED BY THE COMMIT UNDER REVIEW, AND UNSEEN BY REVIEWER B. ci.yml's new step ends `--branch "$PR_HEAD_REF"`, with PR_HEAD_REF supplied via `env:`. That indirection is a correct fix for F5's shell-injection concern (head.ref is PR-author-controlled free text) and is worth keeping. But `$VAR` is POSIX-shell syntax, and this step lives in job `test`, whose matrix is os [windows-latest, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest] x python ["3.10","3.12"]. There is NO `shell:` key anywhere in .github/workflows/ci.yml (verified by grep -- zero matches), so the two windows-latest legs run this step under the runner default, PowerShell. In PowerShell an environment variable is $env:PR_HEAD_REF; a bare $PR_HEAD_REF is an undefined PowerShell variable and interpolates to the empty string. So on Windows the step effectively runs `--branch ""`, args.branch is "" (not None, so _current_branch/$GITHUB_HEAD_REF is never consulted as fallback), and since load_exemptions validates `branch` as a NON-EMPTY string, no entry can ever match: branch-based exemptions are SILENTLY INERT on the Windows legs, while pr-based exemptions still work. This is exactly the "silently inert plumbing" shape -- and note it is fail-safe, not fail-open for injection (empty is harmless), so the F5 fix is not undone. Impact TODAY is nil: acceptance_exempt.json ships `[]`, and the step is continue-on-error report-only. Impact LATER is real: the same PR would report EXEMPT on ubuntu/macOS and a non-exempt outcome on Windows, and if this gate is armed to block without fixing it, the Windows legs would fail a legitimately exempt deliverable. Fix is one line: `shell: bash` on that step. I ALSO NOTE HONESTLY: I could not execute this leg -- no pwsh on this container (`which pwsh powershell` -> nothing), and I did not trigger a Windows CI run. This is reasoned from the PowerShell/Actions-default-shell semantics plus the verified absence of any `shell:` key, not measured.

F2 -- WRONG QUANTITATIVE CLAIM, shipped in the module docstring. scripts/lwb_check_acceptance_criteria.py's closing docstring says it "returns one of six exit codes -- see `ACCEPTANCE_EXIT_*` below". There are FIVE ACCEPTANCE_EXIT_* constants (PASS=0, FAIL=1, UNVERIFIABLE=2, NO_RANGE=3, CONFIG_ERROR=4) and five distinct values. The PR body compounds it: "Six outcomes, six distinct exit-code buckets" -- there are SEVEN Outcome members (PASS, EXEMPT, FAIL, NO_ISSUE_REFERENCE, UNVERIFIABLE, NO_RANGE, CONFIG_ERROR) mapping onto five buckets. Both numbers are wrong, and the body's own next sentence enumerates the five correctly, as does the test, which is literally named test_all_seven_outcomes_map_to_the_documented_exit_codes. Measured: `len(list(Outcome))` == 7, `sorted(set(_OUTCOME_EXIT_CODE.values()))` == [0,1,2,3,4]. Documentation only -- behaviour and the mapping test are correct.

F3 -- UNDOCUMENTED SEMANTICS + UNTESTED CASE in the exemption mechanism, resolving to the BROADER reading. The docstring says each entry "matches a PR number or a branch name (or both -- see below)" and never says, below or anywhere, whether an entry carrying BOTH fields is a conjunction or a disjunction. _find_exemption is a disjunction. Measured directly: with entries=[{"pr":70,"branch":"scoping-spike"}], _find_exemption exempts (70,"scoping-spike"), (70,"totally-unrelated-branch") AND (99,"scoping-spike"). No test covers the both-fields case (grep for "both" in the test file finds only the both-NULL rejection). An author writing both fields to NARROW an exemption to "that PR on that branch" silently gets a strictly wider one: that PR on any branch, plus any PR on that branch. For an opt-out whose entire safety argument is that it is narrow and reviewable, the ambiguity should be resolved in prose and pinned by a test whichever way is intended. Nil impact today (file ships empty).

F4 -- STALE MEASUREMENT in the PR body and proof/68.json. Both record `633 passed`. At the reviewed head the true count is 635: the head commit f65fd7f6 added two tests to tests/test_lwb_check_acceptance_criteria.py (24 -> 26 test defs, verified with `git show 8a577b0:...` vs the working file). The 633 figure is a true measurement of 8a577b0 that was not refreshed for the final commit; f65fd7f6's own commit message does say 635, so the commit is honest and it is the PR body and proof record that lag. proof/68.json also carries `commit: 2b83009e`, so its scope is at least stated.

F5 -- TENSE/STATE CLAIM about another PR, wrong as written. The module docstring says the same defect "is exactly what this repo's own resolve_reviewable_head in scripts/lwb_lanes.py already had to fix once (its own --first-parent correction, tracked as this repo's PR #63)", and the PR body says "already fixed once". It is not fixed: on origin/main, resolve_reviewable_head still runs `["git","log","--format=%H",head_sha]` with no --first-parent (verified by reading origin/main:scripts/lwb_lanes.py), and PR #63 is state=open, merged=false (verified by REST). Mitigating, and why this is a note rather than a charge: the text names PR #63 explicitly so a reader can check, and the reasoning is correctly reused here regardless of #63's merge status -- lwb_check_acceptance_criteria.py uses --first-parent from the outset and has a test that fails without it (probe 1). Worth correcting because this repo's whole state-claims discipline exists to stop "already fixed" being written about work that has not landed, and lwb_check_state_claims.py only scans HANDOFF.md, so it cannot catch this one.

=== ASSESSMENT ===
AGREE. The deliverable does what it says: the comparison logic is correct against real GitHub data, every guard I tried to collapse was held in place by a failing test, the six/seven distinct outcomes keep "could not check" apart from "checked and passed", the gh-unauthenticated-in-CI limitation and the report-only posture are disclosed in the PR body and the docstring rather than hidden, and the two D24 design gaps are answered with reasons rather than hand-waved. Every gate script I could run passes. F1 is the only finding with teeth and it is latent behind an empty exemption file and continue-on-error; it must be fixed (one `shell: bash`) before this gate is armed, and I would rather see it fixed here than tracked, but it does not make a report-only step wrong to land. F2-F5 are documentation and stale-number corrections.
